chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Make the A7 shape
exercises.purpose: Land the 7th voicing that walks up from E7.

params.fingers: index(1) on D-string 2nd fret, ring(3) on B-string 2nd fret, low E muted
params.strings_played: A, D, G, B, high e (low E stays quiet)

exercises.coaching: A7 is a small triangle in the middle of the neck: index on the D string second fret, ring on the B string second fret. Keep the low E quiet. That 7th note is the open G string — it is what lifts this chord out of plain A. Tiny shape, big sound.

exercises.name: One clean down-strum
exercises.purpose: Strum the five ringing strings without catching the muted low E.

params.action: single downward strum, relaxed wrist, skip the low E
params.cue: listen for the open G-string 7th colour

exercises.coaching: Hold A7 and strum down — but let the pick fall just past the low E so it stays silent. Loose wrist. Listen for the open G string; that is the 7. Buzz on the B or D? Press a touch closer to the fret. That clean A7 is the second colour of the blues.

exercises.name: E7 to A7 walk
exercises.purpose: Practice the most common blues change, slowly, in time.

params.cue: one chord per 4 beats, change on the downbeat

exercises.coaching: Now walk: E7 for four beats, A7 for four. One chord per four beats, change right on the click. The metronome is slow so you can land clean. This E7-to-A7 move is in thousands of blues tunes — you just met it.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Second colour of the blues: A7. Small shape, but it walks you right out of E7 and into a real progression.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: A7 is a triangle in the middle: index on D second fret, ring on B second fret, low E quiet. The open G string is your 7th note — that lift is the sound.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Strum down but let the pick fall past the low E so it stays silent. Loose wrist. Listen for the open G string. Buzz? Closer to the fret. That clean A7 is the second blues colour.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: Walk it: E7 four beats, A7 four beats, on the click. Slow metronome. That E7-to-A7 move is in countless blues songs — you just met it.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can change E7 to A7 on the beat, you have the backbone of a 12-bar. Two colours down, one to go.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: E7 and A7 in your hands, walking in time. Lesson 3 of the pack adds B7 and you play a full 12-bar blues. For real.

lesson.title: Blues Pack 2 — The A7 Chord (walking up from E7)
lesson.one_line_promise: A7 + the E7 walk gives you the backbone of a 12-bar.
objectives: Form A7 (index on D 2nd, ring on B 2nd, low E muted)
Strum it clean, skipping the muted low E
Walk E7 to A7 on the beat at a slow shuffle tempo

free_metronome: hold the E7-A7 walk tempo (swing feel)
